[#examples]
= Examples
:idprefix: examples_

All the following examples can be found in the `examples/` folder of this library.
We will first start with the basics and then move on to more advanced examples.

[#examples_foundational]
== Foundational Examples

[#examples_construction]
=== Construction

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/construction.cpp[example] demonstrates the many ways to create a `beman::big_int`: from built-in integers, from floating-point values, from a user-defined literal, by copy and move, and from a range of limbs
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$construction.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
zero:         0
from_int:     -123456789
from_ull:     18446744073709551615
from_double:  1000000000000000
truncated:    -42
from_literal: 170141183460469231731687303715884105728

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_operators]
=== Fundamental operators

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/operators.cpp[example] demonstrates the fundamental arithmetic, comparison, bitwise, shift, increment, and compound-assignment operators of `beman::big_int`
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$operators.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
sum:        1000000000007
difference: 999999999993
product:    7000000000000
quotient:   142857142857 remainder 1
complement: -1000000000001
2^100:      1267650600228229401496703205376

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_factorial]
=== Factorial

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/factorial.cpp[example] demonstrates computing the 100th factorial with `beman::big_int` using ordinary arithmetic operators in a recursive function
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$factorial.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
fact_100:
93326215443944152681699238856266700490715968264381621468592963895217599993229915608941463976156518286253697920827223758251185210916864000000000000000000000000

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_literals]
=== User-defined literals

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/literals.cpp[example] demonstrates writing `beman::big_int` constants directly in source code with the `_n` and `_N` literal suffixes, including non-decimal bases, digit separators, and negative values
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$literals.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
big:      340282366920938463463374607431768211457
from_hex: 255
negative: -1000000000000000000000

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_charconv]
=== Numeric conversions

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/charconv.cpp[example] demonstrates parsing a `beman::big_int` from text with `from_chars` and rendering it back with `to_chars`, including the `to_chars` overload that takes the value over
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$charconv.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
decimal: 340282366920938463463374607431768211457
hex:     100000000000000000000000000000001

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_string]
=== String conversions

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/string.cpp[example] demonstrates rendering a `beman::big_int` to a `std::string` with `to_string` and to a `std::wstring` with `to_wstring`, including the overloads that take the value over
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$string.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
decimal:  340282366920938463463374607431768211456
hex:      100000000000000000000000000000000
negative: -100000000000000000000000000000000

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_numeric]
=== Numeric functions

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/numeric.cpp[example] demonstrates the free numeric helpers in `<beman/big_int/numeric.hpp>`: `abs` for the magnitude of a value, `saturating_cast` for range-clamped narrowing to a built-in integer, `in_range` for range checking, `gcd` and `lcm` for the greatest common divisor and least common multiple, and `midpoint` for half the sum of any mix of `big_int` and built-in integer arguments
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$numeric.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
magnitude:   170141183460469231731687303715884105728
owned:       170141183460469231731687303715884105728
clamped_hi:  2147483647
clamped_lo:  -2147483648
clamped_neg: 0
exact:       12345
range:       true
divisor:     55827575822966466661959896531774472192
mixed:       42
coprime:     1
multiple:    4008866564695576038062016250153661299163136
mixed_lcm:   3070516670263155666407794309247595970560
split:       true
between:     182528259153188862751277881710636636831744
halfway:     307051667026315566640779430924759597056
rounds_first:true

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_limits]
=== Numeric limits

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/limits.cpp[example] demonstrates the `std::numeric_limits` specialization in `<beman/big_int/limits.hpp>`: what it reports for an unbounded type, why `is_bounded` rather than `max()` is the member to test, and how a single template can serve `big_int` and a built-in integer alike
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$limits.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
int32_t range: -2147483648 .. 2147483647
big_int range: unbounded

digits:        2147483647
digits10:      646456992
max_digits10:  646456994

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_division]
=== Integer division

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/division.cpp[example] demonstrates the `div_rem_to_zero` free function, which computes the quotient and remainder together in a single division
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$division.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
dividend:  100000000000000000000000000000000
divisor:   1000000007
quotient:  99999999300000004899999
remainder: 965700007

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_io]
=== Formatting and output

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/io.cpp[example] demonstrates displaying a `beman::big_int` by converting it to text with `to_string` and by formatting it with `std::format`
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$io.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
decimal: 340282366920938463463374607431768211456
hex:     100000000000000000000000000000000
format {:#x}:  0x100000000000000000000000000000000
format {:b}:   101010
format {:>12}: '         255'
format {:+}:   +7

result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_advanced]
== Advanced Examples

[#examples_fibonacci]
=== Fibonacci

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/fibonacci.cpp[example] demonstrates computing the 10,000th Fibonacci number with `beman::big_int` using fast matrix exponentiation by squaring
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$fibonacci.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
fib_10000:


result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_roots]
=== Roots

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/roots.cpp[example] demonstrates computing the exact integer square root and cube root of a 1,001-digit integer with `beman::big_int`
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$roots.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
result_sqrt:


result_cbrt:


result_is_ok: true
----
====

[#examples_rsa]
=== RSA

.This https://github.com/eisenwave/std-big-int/blob/main/examples/rsa.cpp[example] demonstrates the usage of `beman::big_int` in the RSA algorithm
====
[source, c++]
----
include::example$rsa.cpp[]
----

.Expected Output
[listing]
----
message:
Hello std-big-int RSA

recover:
Hello std-big-int RSA

result_is_ok: true
----
